Kolecto est une fintech de gestion affiliée au Groupe Crédit Agricole qui simplifie, sécurise et améliore les finances des TPE-PME françaises, en conformité avec les dernières réglementations en vigueur.

Projet hybride par essence, notre solution digitale et humaine s'évertue à prendre le meilleur de deux mondes complémentaires : la culture agile et la vélocité d'une startup combinées à la puissance d'une banque universelle de proximité de 140 ans, leader européen historique de son industrie.

Aujourd’hui, Kolecto, c’est une équipe de 140 personnes qui évolue dans un environnement de travail très dynamique, avec des bureaux idéalement situés à Miromesnil (Paris 8e), à 5 min des Champs-Elysées et 10 min de la gare Saint-Lazare.

📌 Notre mission

Travailler chez Kolecto, c'est prendre activement part à un mouvement qui nous dépasse, celui de soutenir le maximum de TPE-PME de notre tissu économique, et notamment les plus vulnérables, dans la réussite de leurs transitions : technologique, économique et réglementaire.

Nous nous engageons au quotidien pour amplifier le pouvoir de projection et d’action des entrepreneurs, dirigeants et employés de TPE-PME qui contribuent à la compétitivité et la modernisation de notre pays.

🚀 Notre ambition

Avec le soutien du Groupe Crédit Agricole et de son réseau national historique (39 Caisses Régionales, 7000 conseillers) ainsi que du réseau LCL (1100+ conseillers), Kolecto est en forte croissance et vise à accompagner la digitalisation de plus de 500 000 entreprises sur les prochaines années, en assumant sa fonction de pont durable entre la banque de proximité, les experts-comptables et l’écosystème de partenaires de confiance des TPE-PME.

  • La puissance de notre mission : nous trouvons beaucoup de sens à servir le maximum de TPE-PME françaises, et notamment celles qui sont traditionnellement le plus à la marge des dernières vagues de digitalisation et modernisation du pays ;

  • Notre politique de télétravail flexible, qui permet jusqu'à 3 jours de télétravail par semaine en France.
  • Nos événements internes fédérateurs : deux séminaires par an, talks inspirants, afterworks, etc.

🎯 Votre mission

Développement d'applications frontend : Concevoir, développer et maintenir des interfaces utilisateur réactives et accessibles en utilisant des technologies modernes telles que React, TypeScript, HTML5 et CSS3.

Collaboration inter-équipes : Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les équipes backend, produit et mobile pour assurer une intégration fluide et cohérente entre les différents composants.

Optimisation des performances : Améliorer la performance des applications en optimisant le rendu, la gestion de l'état et les appels API.

Veille technologique : Effectuer une veille technologique et proposer des améliorations continues pour adopter les meilleures pratiques et outils du secteur.

Encadrement technique : Encadrer et accompagner techniquement les développeurs juniors de l’équipe, en les orientant sur les standards de qualité et les bonnes pratiques de développement frontend.

🙌 Ce que nous offrons

Chez Kolecto, on est convaincus que bien travailler, c’est avant tout avoir les bonnes conditions : de la flexibilité, du confort et des avantages concrets qui font vraiment la différence.

Chez Kolecto, la tech se construit au quotidien par celles et ceux qui la font vivre. Découvrez les témoignages de nos équipes techniques :

Wir bauen die Software, mit der Mieterstromprojekte laufen: Zählerdaten rein, Abrechnung raus, und alles dazwischen. Das Core Team verantwortet das Betreiberportal, das Produkt, auf dem der laufende Betrieb unserer Kunden steht. Es ist unser fachlich tiefstes Team, und es wächst.

Dafür suchen wir eine Person, die das Team führt und das Geschäft dahinter versteht. Nicht als Durchreiche für Tickets und nicht als Architekt, der alles selbst entscheidet, sondern als jemand, der Business-Anforderungen in technische Entscheidungen übersetzt und dafür sorgt, dass gute Entwickler gute Arbeit machen können: klare Ziele, wenig Reibung, ehrliches Feedback, verlässliche Lieferung.

NetBox Labs is seeking a Full Stack Engineer to join our rapidly expanding engineering team. We have multiple positions open at different seniority levels across several teams.

About NetBox Labs

NetBox Labs builds the next generation of network automation tools for modern infrastructure teams, with NetBox as the network source of truth at the center. The Observability team builds the products that connect that source of truth to what is actually running on the network:

  • NetBox Discovery finds devices, interfaces, and other network entities.

  • NetBox Assurance brings discovered data into NetBox and helps operators spot drift between intended and actual state, review changes, and decide what to accept.

  • Fleet Management and the Orb agent deploy, configure, and manage the agents that collect discovery and telemetry data from customer networks. These agents use SNMP, gNMI, and other device interfaces.

  • Diode is the ingestion pipeline that moves that data into NetBox reliably.

We're hiring a Full Stack Engineer who can work across the whole path, from the agents and services that collect network data to the interfaces operators use to understand and act on it.

Role overview

You'll join the Observability team and take ownership of features end to end. That covers:

  • Go and Python services and gRPC APIs in the control and data planes.

  • The data flows that carry discovery and telemetry results into NetBox.

  • The React dashboards and interfaces where customers monitor network and device health, explore telemetry, review discovered data, and manage their agent fleet.

You'll work closely with product, design, and other engineering teams, and you'll help run the services the team owns in production.

This role is hands-on. You'll ship features across the stack, improve reliability and performance, and help define the architecture and practices needed to scale network discovery and assurance to large, complex customer environments.

What you'll do

  • Design, build, and operate backend services in Go and Python for discovery, assurance, fleet management, and data ingestion.

  • Define and evolve gRPC and REST APIs with clear, versioned contracts using Protocol Buffers and OpenAPI.

  • Build React and TypeScript monitoring and telemetry dashboards that show device, interface, and network health in real time, with time-series charts, status views, and drill-down from fleet to device to interface.

  • Design dashboard experiences that help operators spot problems fast: sensible defaults, time-range and filter controls, thresholds and alert states, and clear links from a metric to the underlying device in NetBox.

  • Work with backend engineers on the query and aggregation APIs that power dashboards, so they stay fast with large fleets and high-frequency telemetry.

  • Build type-safe integration between frontend and backend using generated API clients, shared schemas, and consistent error and auth handling.

  • Participate in the team's on-call rotation for the services it owns.

  • Add automated tests across the stack (unit, integration, contract, and end-to-end) and enforce quality gates in CI.

  • Collaborate with product managers, designers, customer-facing teams, and other engineering teams. The goal is for features to solve real network operator problems.

  • Use AI-enabled development tools and agentic workflows day to day to speed up design, coding, testing, code review, and incident triage, and help the team adopt them effectively and safely.

  • Review code, mentor teammates, and share best practices for service design, API design, and frontend engineering.

  • Participate in planning processes and help shape the roadmap.

What we're looking for (minimum qualifications)

  • Experience: 5+ years of professional software engineering, with meaningful production experience on both backend and frontend.

  • Backend:

    • Production experience with Go and Python: strong in at least one and working proficiency in the other.

    • Hands-on experience designing and operating gRPC services with Protocol Buffers, including schema evolution and backward compatibility, streaming RPCs, deadlines, interceptors/middleware, and error handling.

    • Experience building distributed, event-driven systems, including message queues (e.g., RabbitMQ or Kafka), asynchronous job processing, and idempotent data ingestion.

  • Frontend (monitoring and telemetry dashboards):

    • Strong React and TypeScript skills, including component composition, state management, and typing best practices.

    • Proven experience building monitoring, observability, or analytics dashboards: time-series charts, heatmaps, status and health views, and drill-down navigation.

    • Hands-on experience with data visualization libraries (e.g., D3, ECharts, Recharts, uPlot, or Visx).

    • Experience rendering large or high-frequency datasets performantly, using techniques such as downsampling, virtualization, and canvas or WebGL rendering.

    • Experience handling real-time data in the browser via WebSockets, server-sent events, or gRPC-Web streaming, along with caching and refresh strategies (e.g., TanStack Query).

    • Modern CSS (TailwindCSS or similar utility-first frameworks), responsive layout, and practical accessibility (WCAG), including color-blind-safe palettes and accessible charts.

    • Automated frontend testing with Jest and React Testing Library, including visual regression testing for charts and dashboards.

  • AI-enabled development:

    • Practical, regular use of AI coding assistants and agents (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot) across the development lifecycle: writing and refactoring code, generating tests, reviewing changes, and writing documentation.

    • Good judgment about when to trust AI output, including verifying generated code, keeping changes reviewable, and protecting sensitive data such as customer network information and credentials.

    • Familiarity with prompting and context techniques that make AI tools effective on a real codebase, such as project instructions, specs, and structured workflows.

  • Ways of working:

    • Good communication skills and a proven ability to work collaboratively in small, cross-functional teams.

    • Comfortable working in a fast-moving environment and contributing to product and technical decisions.

Nice to have

  • Networking protocols and device interfaces:

    • Familiarity with networking protocols and concepts such as TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, BGP, OSPF, VLANs, and LLDP/CDP.

    • Experience with network management and telemetry interfaces such as SNMP (MIBs, polling, traps), gNMI/gNOI, streaming telemetry.

  • Network automation: Experience with NetBox, network automation frameworks (e.g., NAPALM, Nornir, Netmiko), or building agents that run in customer environments.

  • Telemetry and observability: OpenTelemetry/OTLP, Prometheus, or time-series databases (e.g., Mimir, InfluxDB, ClickHouse), including query languages such as PromQL.

  • Dashboard tooling:

Warum LPE Immobilien?

  • Die Hausverwaltung ist der unterschätzteste Beruf Deutschlands: Kein anderer entscheidet so unmittelbar darüber, wie Menschen wohnen. Trotzdem gilt der Hausverwalter bis heute als Buchhalter mit Schlüsselbund. Wir wollen das ändern, und Software ist dafür einer unserer zentralen Hebel.
  • Mit lpeOS bauen wir die Systeme, mit denen wir selbst jeden Tag arbeiten: das Kundenportal für unsere Eigentümer, KI-Agenten, die eigenständig Aufgaben übernehmen, und das Verwaltercockpit als Arbeitsumgebung unserer Verwalter. Wir digitalisieren unsere eigenen Prozesse, um die Arbeit unserer Verwalter jeden Tag ein Stück besser zu machen, mit dem Anspruch, die Branche zu revolutionieren.
  • Für Design ist das ein seltener Ausgangspunkt: Kaum eine Branche wurde von moderner Software so lange übersehen. Für diese Berufe hat noch nie jemand ernsthaft gestaltet. Du wärst die erste Design-Person in unserem neuen Produktteam und baust Design-System und Designprozess mit auf.


Was dich bei uns erwartet – Deine Aufgaben

  • Wir arbeiten als ein Team von Product Engineers, manche technischer, manche gestalterischer. Du wärst die gestalterischste Person, arbeitest aber im selben Repository und Rhythmus wie alle anderen. Was du gestaltest, ist meist wenige Wochen später live.
  • Du verantwortest den Designprozess von Anfang bis Ende: Du führst Interviews mit Verwaltern und Eigentümern, verdichtest die Erkenntnisse zu Konzepten und gestaltest daraus Interfaces für Kundenportal und Verwaltercockpit. Deine Kolleginnen, Kollegen und Kunden sind direkt erreichbar, Feedback bekommst du auf kurzem und direktem Weg.
  • Deine Designs bleiben nicht in Figma: Mit KI-gestützter Entwicklung (React, Tailwind, shadcn/ui) bringst du sie selbst ins Frontend und setzt Teil-Features, teils auch ganze Features, gemeinsam mit dem Team um. Du musst kein Programmierer sein, aber du willst, dass deine Arbeit im Produkt landet, und legst dafür selbst Hand an.
  • Ein besonderes Feld ist Design für KI-Agenten: Du gestaltest Interaktionsmuster für Workflows, in denen Agenten Aufgaben übernehmen. Wo braucht der Nutzer Kontrolle, wo Transparenz? Muster, für die es noch kaum Vorbilder gibt.


Was du mitbringen solltest

  • 2 bis 5 Jahre Erfahrung im Produktdesign, gern mit B2B-Software oder komplexen Workflows.
  • Ein Portfolio mit 2 bis 3 Case Studies, die deinen Weg von der Nutzerfrage bis zum ausgelieferten Interface zeigen: Deine Denkweise interessiert uns mehr als die Menge an Screens.
  • Sicherer Umgang mit Figma, von Wireframes über klickbare Prototypen bis zur Komponentenbibliothek.
  • Erfahrung mit qualitativem Research: Interviews führen, Erkenntnisse verdichten, Annahmen mit Usability-Tests prüfen.
  • Gespür für Interaction Design und Informationsarchitektur in datenreichen Anwendungen.
  • Gute bis sehr gute Praxis mit KI-gestützter Entwicklung (z. B. Claude Code, Cursor, v0): Du bringst Teil-Features oder ganze Features selbst in den Code.
  • Solide Grundlagen in HTML und CSS, JavaScript ist ein Plus.
  • Deutschkenntnisse mindestens auf B2-Niveau.
Du erfüllst nicht alle Punkte? Bewirb dich trotzdem. Talent und Lernkurve zählen bei uns mehr als Jahreszahlen im Lebenslauf.


Was wir dir bieten

  • Eine seltene Ausgangslage. Wir bauen Software für ein Geschäftsmodell, das bereits funktioniert, und wissen, dass sie gebraucht wird. Du erlebst aus nächster Nähe, wie sich eine ganze Branche neu erfindet, und gestaltest das aktiv mit.
  • Echter Impact. Alles, was du gestaltest, kommt bei unseren Verwaltern, Eigentümern und Kunden direkt zum Einsatz.
  • Eine Branche von innen kennenlernen. Die Immobilienwirtschaft ist einer der größten Märkte Deutschlands und steht erst am Anfang ihrer Digitalisierung. Du lernst sie dort kennen, wo die Entscheidungen fallen.
  • Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit den Produktverantwortlichen. Kurze Wege, schnelle Entscheidungen und jemand, der sich Zeit für deine Fragen nimmt.
  • Mentoring und Weiterentwicklung. Wohin du dich entwickeln willst, Richtung UX Engineering oder Produktverantwortung, besprechen wir offen und regelmäßig. Mentoring ist bei uns in alle Richtungen möglich.
  • Ehrliches Feedback. Sofort und in beide Richtungen.
  • Die richtigen Werkzeuge. Premium-Hardware, cloudbasierte Tools, aktuelles KI-Tooling, papierlos. Wenn dir etwas fehlt, um besser zu arbeiten, bekommst du es.
  • Perspektive. Diese Stelle ist so gebaut, dass sie mit dir und mit lpeOS wächst.

About Gladia

Gladia builds the audio AI infrastructure behind the new generation of voice products. Our mission is to give every voice platform true conversational intelligence — the audio infrastructure that understands every conversation, turning voice into the world's most valuable data layer.

Our API turns real-world conversational audio into accurate, structured, real-time output — powered by our proprietary Solaria ASR, across 100+ languages, with industry-leading latency.

Hundreds of companies build their voice products on Gladia — from meeting assistants and voice agents to sales-enablement and contact-center platforms. We started in Paris, our growth is developer-led and heavily US-driven (and we're going after the US market hard).

Headquartered in vibrant tech hubs like Paris and New York City, Gladia has been by OVH Groupe — Europe's leading cloud provider — and now operates as a fully autonomous brand and company within the Group.

We're guided by four values:

  • Honest — Say the real thing, kindly.

  • Smart — Work smart, ship fast.

  • Builders — Own your scope, build to last.

  • Caring — Support people, take pride in the craft.

The role

AI is at the core of our product — and increasingly at the core of how we design. Our brand runs on a custom system that's prompt-driven and code-native. The depth of this role is in scaling it, keeping our identity sharp and consistent across every touchpoint, extending it into video, and supporting our growing set of internal products.

That means working with a high degree of autonomy. You anticipate needs, reach out directly to the teams you support without waiting to be briefed, and you've already run a brand on your own — comfortable managing external partners when needed, and used to moving fast.

It also means strong web skills are non-negotiable: our website is hand-coded (Next.js, HTML, CSS) in Cursor and hosted on Vercel, so comfort with Cursor or an equivalent IDE is a prerequisite, alongside real fluency and curiosity around AI tools.

What you'll do

  • Own Gladia's brand identity end-to-end across our website, marketing materials, decks, and video

  • Design and build our website directly in code (Next.js, HTML, CSS), working in an IDE like Cursor and shipping through GitHub, deployed on Vercel

  • Operate and extend our AI-powered design system, using prompting as a core creative tool alongside traditional design craft

  • Push our web presence toward richer, more immersive and interactive experiences

  • Extend our visual identity into new formats, in particular video

  • Contribute design support to internal tools such as GladiaFlow and Compare STT

  • Move fast and deliver independently across a wide range of formats

Who you are

  • Senior brand design experience, ideally at a startup, having owned a brand end-to-end rather than executed against an existing brand book

  • A portfolio that shows systems thinking: a cohesive identity with real range across web, video, decks, and brand — not a handful of one-off pieces

  • Fluency with Cursor (or an equivalent IDE), confident enough with code to review and ship changes via GitHub

  • A real, hands-on relationship with AI tools in your design workflow — genuine daily use, not occasional dabbling

  • The ability to build a distinct visual language for a technical, abstract product, without leaning on stock photography or literal product screenshots

  • Sharp, fast decision-making, with the ability to clearly explain the reasoning behind your choices

  • Fluent English

Bonus Point

  • Experience managing external vendors or freelancers

  • Background in B2B SaaS or deep tech, where the product itself is hard to visualize

  • Based in or open to working on-site in Paris, as a big plus

What Gladia Offers

  • Health insurance (100% coverage) and a pension contract for you & your family

  • Flexible vacation policy

About the Role:
CrowdStrike's marketing team is building an agentic AI platform that automates end-to-end workflows. Our mission is to reinvent how marketing works at CrowdStrike, giving teams the power to move faster, create smarter, and drive greater impact.

You will architect and build the infrastructure behind modern marketing execution, from AI agents and orchestration pipelines to unified data foundations, internal tooling, and production-grade integrations. You will turn high-friction workflows into durable operating systems that teams can trust and adopt at scale.

As a Sr. AI Growth Engineer on this team, you'll own the technical foundation of this platform. You'll build the integrations, infrastructure, UIs and tooling that delivers an enterprise-grade system used by marketing teams across CrowdStrike. You'll work directly with marketing leadership to ship production capabilities fast. This role is ideally suited for a builder who can pair product thinking with hands-on execution.

You will embed directly with marketing teams, building alongside the people doing the work to solve real operational pain points. Success in this role is measured not only by what you ship, but by workflows permanently transformed, adoption that sticks, and teams that become increasingly self-sufficient.

This role leads the Marketing Engineering pillar and reports directly to the VP of Marketing Excellence & Transformation. It offers rare greenfield ownership at the intersection of AI, marketing operations, and developer tooling, with direct visibility to senior marketing leadership.

Locations: Preference for candidates in Seattle, WA or located remotely on the West Coast.

  • Build integrations: connecting the AI campaign engine to CrowdStrike's marketing stack - work management platforms (e.g., Workfront), marketing automation systems (e.g., Marketo), collaboration tools (Google Docs, Slack), CMS, and digital asset management systems

  • Design, build, and deploy custom AI agents: and agentic workflows that integrate AI APIs, MCP servers, automation platforms, and enterprise systems into our GTM motion
  • Implement auth, permissions, and multi-tenancy: so multiple marketing teams and campaign owners can run pipelines concurrently with appropriate access controls
  • Own CI/CD and reliability: automated testing for agent outputs, regression detection, deployment pipelines, monitoring and alerting

  • Strong communication skills and a genuine ability to translate technical concepts for non-technical audiences
  • Working knowledge of CI/CD, containerization, cloud infrastructure, and observability (AWS preferred)
